messages:
Priya R: ok team — we need to lock the request/response schema decisions for the next API milestone. primary concerns from customers: (1) consistent token accounting fields that work across chat/completions/embeddings, (2) stable trace / request ids for cross-service debugging, (3) how to expose function/tool call metadata and structured outputs without breaking existing clients.

Samir P: agreed. goal is: minimal breaking changes, clear launch criteria, and a migration path for heavy customers. thinking we make new fields opt-in via a preview header for 1.0 then GA later.

Carlos M: quick note on token fields — runtime needs both per-input-part and per-output-part counts for billing + cost SLOs. propose canonical names: `usage.input_tokens`, `usage.output_tokens`, `usage.total_tokens`. For embeddings we return `usage.input_tokens` (since embeddings have no generation).

Nia K: +1 on canonical names. devex asks that `usage` be present even when zeros (so SDKs can always read it without guard clauses). makes analytics simpler.

Priya R: we also have customer asks for per-prompt token breakdown (system/user/messages) — should we add optional `usage.breakdown`? that would be helpful but potentially expensive to compute.

Carlos M: `usage.breakdown` ok as opt-in flag `X-Usage-Breakdown: true` or query param. runtime can compute only when requested. shape suggestion: `usage.breakdown = [{role: "system", tokens: 8}, {role: "user", tokens: 24}]`

Samir P: good compromise. add to preview only. include cost note in docs: breakdown adds ~5-10% CPU overhead for long contexts. we should hardcore a warning in console.

Priya R: trace ids — customers want a single header/field that travels through our internal services and into customers' logs. we currently have `x-request-id` in front door but internal spans use separate trace ids. proposal: expose `meta.request_id` (immutable per external request) and `meta.trace_id` (links to internal spans). both strings, both returned in response.

Carlos M: implementable. we should standardize format: `rwd-{region}-{hex8}` for request_id and `rwd-trace-{uuid4}` for trace_id. runtime will accept inbound `x-request-id` or `x-trace-id` and return normalized values.

Nia K: SDKs need guidance: prefer `response.meta.request_id` for customer correlation. also add `response.meta.trace_link` with a short clickable URL for console traces (only in Hosted mode).

Priya R: function/tool calling metadata — customers want both the raw tool response and a structured output field we can validate. two options: (A) keep `tool_response` raw and add `structured.output_v1` as validated JSON, or (B) embed `tools` array each entry `{name, raw, structured, confidence}`. thoughts?

Carlos M: option B is more future-proof. single `tools` array lets us support multiple tool calls in one turn. keep `structured` optional and only present when model/tool returned JSON. schema example in docs:```json
"tools": [
  {"name": "wiki_search", "raw": "<text>", "structured": {"title": "", "url": ""}, "confidence": 0.92}
]
```

Samir P: sounds good. add clear validation rules: `structured` must be JSON object, max depth 5, size limit 16KB. if validation fails we return `structured_error` with a normalized code. include in launch checklist.

Priya R: launch criteria checklist (draft):
- schema fields: `usage`, `meta.request_id`, `meta.trace_id`, `tools` array optional
- SDKs parse `usage` and `meta` without opt-in
- `usage.breakdown` behind opt-in header/param
- structured tool output validation + documented error codes
- console links for hosted traces enabled in preview
- backward compatibility tests pass with top 20 customers

Nia K: add observability requirement: retention of `usage` and `meta` for 90 days for paid customers (configurable). also add a per-route flag to enable `usage.breakdown` to prevent noisy global cost hit.

Carlos M: implementation notes: migrating existing endpoints — add new fields to responses alongside old ones. we should not remove any existing top-level fields for GA. telemetry events: emit `schema_change` event when a client first sees preview fields.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: preview/schema-v1 -> canary on prod-1 (namespace: api-preview) at 1782003399

Samir P: timeline — Ship preview to 10% canary next week, collect SDK errors and customer feedback for 2 weeks, then GA after signoff. Priya, can you own customer comms & migration docs?

Priya R: yes. I'll draft migration guide: mapping old token fields -> `usage.*`, examples for embeddings/chat/structured-tools, FAQ on trace correlation. will include sample curl and SDK snippets.

Nia K: I'll update SDKs to default-read `usage` and attach `meta.request_id` as `requestId` in JS/py clients. will also log if `usage.breakdown` present.

Carlos M: I'll add server flags for breakdown and structured validation, and instrumentation counters for extra CPU.

Samir P: great. last thing — make sure cost impact is in the release notes: opt-in features are free but breakdown/structured validations may increase costs for hosted customers. add a metric `extra_cpu_pct` to rollout dashboard.

Priya R: noted. thanks everyone, I'll circulate the draft schema JSON and checklist later today for final thumbs up. :thumbsup:
